mainTopic: Selling an אמה העבריה to relatives, how an עבד עברי leaves and redeems himself, and the ladder of punishment for trading in שביעית produce
overview: The amud opens by finishing רבי אליעזר's teaching that "לאמה" allows a father to sell his daughter even to relatives. A קל וחומר from people of flawed lineage fails, because they can still do יעוד and relatives cannot. The גמרא explains how רבי מאיר learns these laws. It then settles two ברייתות about selling her to the seller's father or son: the רבנן agree to a sale wherever יעוד is possible. Next comes a ברייתא on "בגפו יבא בגפו יצא". רבא says an עבד עברי is not freed by losing a limb, and רב נחמן בר יצחק explains רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's reading: only a married slave may be given a שפחה כנענית. Another ברייתא teaches that an עבד עברי always redeems himself at the lower price. A scholar challenges אביי on why the פסוקים are read leniently, and אביי answers that the Torah is kind to the slave, since buying one is like buying a master. The scholar then quotes רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא's ladder of punishment for trading in שביעית produce. It runs from selling movable property, fields and house, to selling a daughter, borrowing with interest and selling oneself, even to a non-Jew. That ladder continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Completing the teaching that she may be sold to relatives
steps.stepSummary: The last word of רבי אליעזר's derivation: a father may sell his daughter as a maidservant even to relatives.
steps.simpleTranslation: [It teaches that he may sell her] to relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: This one word finishes a sentence from the previous section. רבי אליעזר learns from the פסוק that a father may sell his daughter as a maidservant even to relatives.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A close relative cannot marry her, so the buyer himself can never do יעוד. Even so, רבי אליעזר says the sale itself is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Relatives who are forbidden to marry her (for example, the father's own father)
A Jewish girl sold by her father as a maidservant

phrases.english: to relatives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the derivation that began in the previous section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, a father may sell his daughter as an אמה העבריה even to relatives she cannot marry.

steps.title: Why do we need a verse? A קל וחומר should be enough
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks: if she may be sold to people of flawed lineage, surely she may be sold to relatives, so why is a פסוק needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't this a logical inference? If he may sell her to people of flawed lineage, shouldn't he also be able to sell her to relatives?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges the need for the פסוק. It argues the rule could be learned by simple logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being sold to someone of flawed lineage, whom she is forbidden to marry, is already allowed. So it seems obvious that selling her to a relative should be allowed too. If logic gives us the rule, the פסוק looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it a logical inference? (a standard opening for a קל וחומר)
People of flawed lineage whom she is forbidden to marry, such as a ממזר
An argument from a lighter case to a stricter case

phrases.english: But isn't it a logical inference?
If he may sell her to those of flawed lineage,
shall he not sell her to relatives?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether the derivation in step 1 is needed
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the פסוק "לאמה" to allow selling her to relatives
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קל וחומר from selling to פסולין should already give us the law, which would make the פסוק unnecessary.

steps.title: The קל וחומר fails, so the verse is needed
steps.stepSummary: Selling to פסולין is different, because those buyers can still do יעוד. Relatives cannot, so the פסוק "לאמה" is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What's special about selling her to people of flawed lineage is that if the master wants to designate her for marriage, he can. But can he sell her to relatives, where even if the master wants to designate her, he cannot? So the verse says "as a maidservant," teaching that he may sell her to relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא knocks down the קל וחומר and shows why the פסוק is still needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a buyer of flawed lineage, קידושין still takes effect, even though the marriage is forbidden. So the main goal of the sale, יעוד, is still possible. With a relative, קידושין does not take effect at all, so logic alone cannot allow the sale. Only the word "לאמה" allows it.

keyTerms.meaning: What is special about... (a formula for breaking a קל וחומר)
Designating the maidservant as a wife for the master or his son

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two groups. פסולין are forbidden to marry her, but if they marry her the קידושין still works. קרובים (close relatives) cannot marry her at all, because their קידושין has no effect.

phrases.english: What is special about selling her to those of flawed lineage
is that if he wants to designate her, he can designate her;
shall he then sell her to relatives,
where if he wants to designate her, he cannot designate her?
The verse says "as a maidservant":
phrases.notes: שמות 21:7

phrases.english: this teaches that he may sell her to relatives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 2 by breaking the קל וחומר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Breaking the קל וחומר (פירכא) and restoring the need for the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Selling to relatives could be learned logically from selling to פסולין.
steps.terutzMaskana: פסולין can still do יעוד and relatives cannot, so only the פסוק "לאמה" allows selling her to relatives.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אליעזר, "לאמה" teaches that she may be sold even to relatives, because logic alone cannot get us there: relatives can never do יעוד.

steps.title: How does רבי מאיר learn these laws?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about רבי מאיר, who used "לאמה" for a different teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי מאיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי מאיר handles these laws. This short question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבי מאיר used "לאמה" for another law: that the father may sell her on condition that no יעוד will happen. Since he has already used up that word, the גמרא wants to know where he learns the rules about פסולין and relatives.

phrases.english: And רבי מאיר?
phrases.notes: He's asking: רבי מאיר used "לאמה" for something else, so where does he learn these laws from?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רבי אליעזר's derivation to how רבי מאיר handles the same laws
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Where רבי מאיר learns that she may be sold to פסולין and to relatives, since he uses "לאמה" elsewhere

steps.title: רבי מאיר's sources: פסולין like רבי אליעזר, relatives like the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר learns the law of פסולין from רבי אליעזר's other source. For relatives, he agrees with the רבנן that she may not be sold to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns the law of flawed lineage from the same place רבי אליעזר learns it. About relatives, he holds like the רבנן, who say he may not sell her to relatives.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about רבי מאיר by splitting it into two parts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For פסולין, רבי מאיר does not need "לאמה", because there is another source that רבי אליעזר also uses. For relatives, he does not need any source at all, since he agrees with the רבנן that such a sale is not allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: From the same place that (someone else) derives it

phrases.english: Regarding those of flawed lineage,
he derives it from the place
from which רבי אליעזר derives it.
phrases.notes: This points back to רבי אליעזר's separate source for פסולין, not the word "לאמה".

phrases.english: Regarding relatives,
he holds like the Rabbis
who say he may not sell her to relatives.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִפְסוּלִין נָפְקָא לֵיהּ מֵהֵיכָא דְּנָפְקָא לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר learns the law of פסולין from רבי אליעזר's other source, and for relatives he holds like the רבנן that she may not be sold to them.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: selling her to פסולין is allowed (from another source), but selling her to relatives is not allowed, like the רבנן.

steps.title: Two ברייתות disagree about selling her to his father or son
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא allows selling her to the father's own father but not to his son. Another ברייתא forbids both.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: He may sell her to his father, but not to his son. Another ברייתא teaches: He may sell her neither to his father nor to his son.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two ברייתות that seem to contradict each other. This sets up the next question about who holds each view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "His father" is the girl's grandfather, and "his son" is her brother. Both are relatives she cannot marry. Even so, one ברייתא treats the two differently.

keyTerms.meaning: It is taught in one ברייתא
To his (the seller's) father / to his son

phrases.english: It is taught in one ברייתא:
He may sell her to his father,
phrases.notes: "His father" means the seller's father, who is the girl's grandfather.

phrases.english: but he may not sell her to his son.
And it is taught in another ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מוֹכְרָהּ לֹא לְאָבִיו וְלֹא לִבְנוֹ.
phrases.english: He may sell her neither to his father nor to his son.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings new sources about specific relatives, building on the dispute over selling to relatives
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two conflicting ברייתות: one allows a sale to his father but not to his son, and the other forbids both.

steps.title: Whose view is the ברייתא that allows his father but not his son?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that forbids both fits the רבנן. But who holds that he may sell her to his father and not to his son?
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, "he may sell her neither to his father nor to his son" fits the רבנן. But "he may sell her to his father but not to his son": whose view is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא matches the first ברייתא to the רבנן. It then asks who could hold the second, mixed view, and sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן forbid selling her to any relative, so the ברייתא that forbids both is easy to explain. רבי אליעזר allows selling to all relatives, so he would allow both. That leaves the split ruling with no clear author.

phrases.aramaic: בִּשְׁלָמָא אֵינוֹ מוֹכְרָהּ לֹא לְאָבִיו וְלֹא לִבְנוֹ –
phrases.english: Granted, "he may sell her neither to his father nor to his son"
is like the Rabbis.
But "he may sell her to his father
but may not sell her to his son":
whose view is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא אֵינוֹ מוֹכְרָהּ לֹא לְאָבִיו וְלֹא לִבְנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the two ברייתות of step 6 to find who holds each view
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that she may be sold to the seller's father but not to his son

steps.title: This ברייתא fits neither side
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא that allows selling to the father's father but not to his son fits neither the רבנן nor רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: It doesn't match the רבנן, and it doesn't match רבי אליעזר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the question from Step 7 and makes it sharper. This ברייתא seems to match no known opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן forbid selling her to any relative, and רבי אליעזר allows selling her to every relative. A ruling that splits the relatives, allowing one and forbidding another, seems to have no author. This sets up the answer in the next step.

phrases.english: It is not in accordance with the Rabbis
and not in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes and sharpens the question of Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא allowing sale to the father's father but not to the son
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both known positions treat all relatives the same way, so a split ruling seems to have no author.

steps.title: The רבנן agree when יעוד is possible
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא really follows the רבנן, who agree that the sale works wherever יעוד is still possible.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it follows the רבנן. The רבנן agree that the sale works where there is a possibility of יעוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא follows the רבנן after all. The רבנן only forbid a sale where יעוד is impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her grandfather cannot marry her himself. He can still designate her for his other son, who is her uncle and is allowed to marry her. Her brother has no such option, so selling her to him stays forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually; signals that the original assumption holds after all
A possibility of designating her for marriage

steps.whatToRemember: For the רבנן, what matters is whether יעוד is possible, either for the buyer himself or for his son. It does not matter whether the buyer himself can marry her.

phrases.english: Actually, it is in accordance with the Rabbis;
the Rabbis concede
where there is a possibility of designation.
phrases.notes: The grandfather can't marry her, but he can designate her for his other son, her uncle.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the רבנן's ban to cases where no יעוד is possible
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן forbid a sale to every relative
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן allow it where the buyer can designate her for his son, such as her grandfather designating her for her uncle

steps.title: Two readings of בגפו יבא בגפו יצא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא gives two readings of the פסוק about an עבד עברי: 'with his body' and 'alone'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'If he comes in בגפו, he shall leave בגפו.' This means he came in with his body and leaves with his body. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: he came in alone and leaves alone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It brings a ברייתא with two ways to read the word בגפו in the פסוק about an עבד עברי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא reads בגפו like בגופו, 'with his body.' רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads it as 'alone,' meaning single. The next steps explain what each reading means in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: A word in the פסוק read as 'with his body' or 'alone'

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
"If he comes in begappo
phrases.notes: שמות 21:3

phrases.english: he shall leave begappo" —
he enters with his body, he shall leave with his body.
phrases.notes: This reading treats בגפו as if it said בגופו, 'his body.'

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
He enters alone, he shall leave alone.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״אִם בְּגַפּוֹ יָבֹא בְּגַפּוֹ יֵצֵא״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about the עבד עברי
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are two readings of בגפו: 'with his body' (תנא קמא) and 'alone' (רבי אליעזר בן יעקב)

steps.title: What does 'with his body' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the practical meaning of the תנא קמא's reading.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'he came in with his body, he leaves with his body' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what practical law the first reading teaches. It is setting up רבא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'with his body' does not tell us any ruling by itself. The גמרא wants to know what this reading changes in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: What is / what does it mean

phrases.english: What is: He enters with his body
he shall leave with his body?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the first opinion in Step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical law behind 'with his body'

steps.title: רבא: he is not freed by losing a limb
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that an עבד עברי does not go free through ראשי אברים, the way an עבד כנעני does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: this teaches that he does not go free through the loss of limbs, like an עבד כנעני does.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question. The עבד עברי leaves the same way he came in, even if his body was injured.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עבד כנעני goes free if his master knocks out his eye or tooth. רבא says the reading 'with his body' tells us this rule does not apply to an עבד עברי.

keyTerms.meaning: The tips of the limbs, like an eye, tooth, or fingers
Here, an עבד כנעני (a non-Jewish slave)

phrases.english: Rava said:
To say that he is not released
through the loss of extremities, like a slave.
phrases.notes: An עבד כנעני goes free if his master knocks out his eye or tooth (שמות 21:26-27).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: לוֹמַר שֶׁאֵינוֹ יוֹצֵא בְּרָאשֵׁי אֵבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An עבד עברי is not freed through loss of limbs

steps.title: אביי: that rule comes from another פסוק
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that this rule is already learned from 'לא תצא כצאת העבדים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: that rule comes from 'She shall not go out as the slaves go out.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא. He says the rule already has its own source, so the פסוק of בגפו is not needed for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about the אמה העבריה already says she does not leave the way עבדים כנענים leave. That covers the limb rule too. So why would בגפו be needed to teach it again?

keyTerms.meaning: She shall not go out as the slaves go out

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
That is derived from: "She shall not go out
phrases.notes: שמות 21:7

phrases.english: as the men slaves do."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: הָהוּא מִ״לֹּא תֵצֵא כְּצֵאת הָעֲבָדִים״ נָפְקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer in Step 12
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reading of בגופו נכנס בגופו יצא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If another פסוק already teaches the rule, the reading of בגפו would add nothing.

steps.title: Without בגפו, we'd think he gets paid and goes free
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that the other פסוק alone might mean he goes free and also gets paid for the eye, so בגפו is still needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had that פסוק, I would have said: the master should pay him the value of his eye and let him go free. The פסוק of בגפו teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his reading. The פסוק of 'לא תצא' could be read the wrong way, so בגפו is needed to make the rule clear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'She does not go out like the slaves' could mean she gets more than an עבד כנעני: payment for the injury plus freedom. בגפו makes clear that he is not freed at all through the injury. He only receives payment for the damage.

keyTerms.meaning: If it were only from there

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the עבד עברי gets nothing for his injury. He still gets paid. He simply does not go free because of it.

phrases.english: If it were from there, I would say:
let him give him the value of his eye
and let him go free;
it teaches us.
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק of בגפו teaches us he does not go free this way at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge in Step 13
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the second פסוק blocks a wrong reading of the first
steps.terutzHavaAmina: He gets the value of the eye and also goes free
steps.terutzMaskana: He is not freed through loss of limbs at all

steps.title: What does 'leaves alone' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's reading and asks what 'leaves alone' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: he came in alone, he leaves alone. What does 'he leaves alone' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the second opinion in the ברייתא. It repeats his words in order to ask what they mean, setting up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Alone' is unclear. It could be talking about his family, or about something else. The גמרא needs to know what practical law it creates.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
He enters alone, he shall leave alone.
What is: He shall leave alone?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the second opinion of Step 10

steps.title: Only a married עבד עברי may be given a שפחה כנענית
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains: if he has a wife and children, his master may give him a שפחה כנענית. If not, he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said, this is what he means: if he has a wife and children, his master may give him a שפחה כנענית. If he has no wife and children, his master may not give him a שפחה כנענית.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains the meaning of 'alone.' It is about whether the master may give the slave a שפחה כנענית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slave who came in 'alone,' with no wife and children, must stay that way, so the master may not give him a שפחה כנענית. Only one who came in with a family may be given one.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he is saying

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, 'alone' means a single עבד עברי may not be given a שפחה כנענית. Only one with a wife and children may.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said
this is what he is saying:
If he has a wife and children,
his master may provide him with a Canaanite maidservant;
if he has no wife and children,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין רַבּוֹ מוֹסֵר לוֹ שִׁפְחָה כְּנַעֲנִית.
phrases.english: his master may not provide him with a Canaanite maidservant.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A master may give a שפחה כנענית only to an עבד עברי who has a wife and children

steps.title: Value went up: he still pays based on the original price
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if a slave was bought for a מנה and his value rose to two hundred, his redemption is figured only on the original מנה, learned from 'מכסף מקנתו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: if he was sold for one hundred and became worth two hundred, how do we know we only count one hundred for him? Because the פסוק says: 'from the money he was bought for.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new ברייתא about an עבד עברי who wants to buy back his remaining years. Its first case is a slave whose value went up while he was working.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the slave redeems himself, he pays for the years he has left. The question is which price we use. The פסוק 'מכסף מקנתו' ties the payment to the price he was bought for, so the higher value does not count against him.

keyTerms.meaning: A unit of money worth one hundred דינרים
We calculate, we figure the amount
From the money he was bought for (ויקרא 25:51)

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
He was sold for one hundred, and he went up in value
and he was now worth two hundred.
From where do we know that we do not calculate for him
phrases.notes: When he buys his freedom, we figure out what he owes for his remaining years.

phrases.english: anything more than one hundred?
Because it says: 'From the money he was bought for.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:51

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נִמְכַּר בְּמָנֶה, וְהִשְׁבִּיחַ וְעָמַד עַל מָאתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא on a new topic, the redemption price of an עבד עברי, after the discussion of בגפו ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the slave went up in value, his redemption is figured on his original purchase price.

steps.title: Value went down: he pays based on the lower, current value
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if he was bought for two hundred and dropped to a מנה, his redemption is figured on the lower מנה, learned from 'כפי שניו'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he was sold for two hundred and became worth one hundred, how do we know we only count one hundred for him? The פסוק says: 'according to his years.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the opposite case: a slave whose value went down. Here too, he only pays the lower amount.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the original price is the higher number, so 'מכסף מקנתו' would hurt the slave. A different פסוק, 'כפי שניו', ties the payment to what his remaining years are worth now. Put the two cases together and the slave always pays the lower amount.
steps.whatToRemember: Whether his value goes up or down, the slave always redeems himself at the lower price.

phrases.english: If he was sold for two hundred and went down in value
and he was now worth one hundred,

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן שֶׁאֵין מְחַשְּׁבִין לוֹ אֶלָּא מָנֶה –
phrases.english: from where do we know that we only calculate one hundred for him?
The פסוק says: 'According to his years.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:52

steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְכַּר בְּמָאתַיִם וְהִכְסִיף וְעָמַד עַל מָנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the mirror case to step 17 and uses a second פסוק so the slave pays the lower amount in both directions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the slave went down in value, his redemption is figured on his current, lower value.

steps.title: These פסוקים are about a slave sold to a נכרי, so what about one sold to a Jew?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא notes that both פסוקים speak of a slave sold to a נכרי, where the Torah is easier on the slave because relatives may redeem him, and asks where we learn the rule for a slave sold to a Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only know this for a slave sold to a non-Jew. Since he can be redeemed by relatives, the owner gets the worse deal. For one sold to a Jew, from where do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא points out a gap: the פסוקים it used are about a slave sold to a נכרי. It is setting up the next step, where it will show the same rule applies to a slave sold to a Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slave sold to a נכרי gets special help: even his relatives can redeem him. So we might say the 'always the lower price' rule is only part of that easier treatment. It would not then carry over to a slave sold to a Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know (this rule for a certain case)
His hand is on the bottom, meaning he gets the worse deal
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: I only know this for a slave
who is sold to a non-Jew,
since he can be redeemed even by relatives,
his hand is on the bottom.
phrases.notes: The owner gets the worse deal: whether the slave's value went up or down, he only collects the lower amount.

phrases.english: If he was sold to a Jew, from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא עֶבֶד הַנִּמְכָּר לְנׇכְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the source of steps 17 and 18 to a slave sold to a נכרי and asks for a source for a slave sold to a Jew.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that the 'lower price' rule also applies to an עבד עברי sold to a Jew.

steps.title: The word 'שכיר' connects the two cases
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that 'שכיר' appears both for a slave sold to a Jew and for one sold to a נכרי, and this גזירה שוה makes the same redemption rule apply to both.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'hired worker' here and 'hired worker' there, to make a גזירה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from step 19. The same word in both sections links them, so the rule for the slave sold to a נכרי also applies to the slave sold to a Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah calls both kinds of slave a 'שכיר', a hired worker. A גזירה שוה tells us to treat the two the same. So the slave sold to a Jew also always redeems himself at the lower price.

keyTerms.meaning: Learning one case from another because the same word appears in both

steps.whatToRemember: Any עבד עברי, whether sold to a נכרי or to a Jew, redeems himself at the lower price. The rule passes from one to the other through the גזירה שוה of 'שכיר'.

phrases.english: The פסוק says 'hired worker,' and again 'hired worker,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:40 (sold to a Jew) and ויקרא 25:53 (sold to a non-Jew).

phrases.english: to teach a גזירה שוה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19 with a גזירה שוה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The shared word 'שכיר' in both sections links them, so the slave sold to a Jew also pays the lower price.

steps.title: אביי invites any question
steps.stepSummary: אביי declares that he is like בן עזאי in the markets of טבריא, ready to answer any question.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: I am like בן עזאי in the markets of טבריא.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי announces that he is ready to answer any question. This sets up the next move, where a scholar takes him up on the offer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן עזאי was known for answering questions sharply in public. By comparing himself to him, אביי opens the floor, and the challenge in the next step follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Here I am / I am hereby

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Here I am like Ben Azzai
phrases.notes: בן עזאי was famous for answering any Torah question on the spot. אביי is saying, 'Ask me anything.'

phrases.english: in the markets of Tiberias.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: הֲרֵינִי כְּבֶן עַזַּאי בְּשׁוּקֵי טְבֶרְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion that will challenge the lenient reading from steps 17-18.

steps.title: Why read the verses leniently?
steps.stepSummary: A scholar asks אביי why the two redemption פסוקים are read in the slave's favor instead of against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the רבנן said to אביי: These verses can be read leniently and can be read stringently. What made you read them leniently? Let us read them stringently!
steps.whatsHappening: A scholar challenges the ברייתא's lenient reading of מכסף מקנתו and כפי שניו. He says the verses could just as easily be read strictly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 17-18 the slave always pays the lower amount. The scholar says the opposite also works: if his value rose, use כפי שניו (his current value), and if it fell, use מכסף מקנתו (the purchase price), so the slave always pays more. Nothing in the verses themselves decides between the two readings.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? Why choose this way over the other?

phrases.english: One of the Rabbis said to Abaye:
After all, these verses
phrases.notes: He means the two פסוקים from before: 'מכסף מקנתו' and 'כפי שניו'.

phrases.english: can be expounded leniently
and can be expounded stringently.
What did you see to expound them leniently?
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: Let us expound them stringently!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי חָזֵית לְמִידְרְשִׁינְהוּ לְקוּלָּא? נִידְרְשִׁינְהוּ לְחוּמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes up אביי's invitation and challenges the derivations of steps 17-18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The lenient reading of מכסף מקנתו and כפי שניו in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two verses could be matched the other way around, so that the slave always pays the higher amount. Nothing forces the lenient reading.

steps.title: The Torah is lenient toward the slave
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the strict reading makes no sense, because the Torah treats the עבד עברי leniently.
steps.simpleTranslation: It cannot enter your mind, since the Merciful One is lenient toward him.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rejects the strict reading. His reason is that the Torah generally goes easy on a Hebrew slave.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי resolves the doubt with the Torah's general attitude toward the slave. If the Torah is generally kind to him, the redemption verses should also be read in his favor. He proves this attitude in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It cannot enter your mind; that idea is impossible
The Torah (the Merciful One) was lenient

phrases.english: It cannot enter your mind,
since the Merciful One is lenient toward him.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ, מִדְּאַקֵּיל רַחֲמָנָא לְגַבֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Uses the Torah's general attitude to decide an unclear reading.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verses could be read either way, so maybe the strict reading is correct.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because the Torah is lenient toward the slave, the verses are read leniently.

steps.title: The slave must live as well as his master
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא on 'כי טוב לו עמך' teaches that the master must give the slave the same food, drink and bed as himself. So buying a slave is like buying a master.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'Because he fares well with you': with you in food and with you in drink. You may not eat fine bread while he eats coarse bread, drink aged wine while he drinks new wine, or sleep on soft bedding while he sleeps on straw. From here they said: anyone who acquires a Hebrew slave is like one who acquires a master for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי brings a ברייתא to prove that the Torah is lenient toward the slave. The master must treat him as an equal in daily living.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'עמך' (with you) teach that the slave's standard of living must match the master's. This shows how much the Torah cares for the slave, which supports reading the redemption verses in his favor.

keyTerms.meaning: Like buying a master for oneself

steps.whatToRemember: An עבד עברי must get the same food, drink and bedding as his master. This is why buying him is called 'buying a master.'
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the classic source for how a master must treat an עבד עברי, and אביי uses it as the reason for the lenient redemption rule.

phrases.english: As it was taught: "Because he fares well with you"
phrases.notes: דברים 15:16

phrases.english: with you in food and with you in drink,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא אַתָּה אוֹכֵל פַּת נְקִיָּה
phrases.english: that you should not be eating fine bread
while he eats coarse bread,
you drinking aged wine
while he drinks new wine,
you sleeping on soft bedding
while he sleeps on straw.
From here they said:
Anyone who acquires a Hebrew slave
is like one who acquires a master for himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim of step 23 that the Torah is lenient toward the slave.
steps.raayaObject: That the Torah treats the עבד עברי leniently.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on 'כי טוב לו עמך' requiring the master to give the slave an equal standard of living.

steps.title: Maybe the kindness covers only food and drink
steps.stepSummary: The scholar argues that the lenient treatment may apply only to daily needs. For redemption we might be strict, based on רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: these words apply to eating and drinking, so that he should not suffer. But regarding redemption, let us be strict with him, based on רבי יוסי son of רבי חנינא.
steps.whatsHappening: The scholar pushes back on אביי's proof. The ברייתא's kindness may be limited to keeping the slave from suffering in daily life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא proves the Torah cares about the slave's comfort, but redemption money is a different matter. The scholar claims there is a reason to be strict on redemption, and he names its source: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.

phrases.english: But say: these words apply
to eating and drinking,
so that he should not suffer,
but regarding redemption, let us be strict with him.
Based on Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: הָנֵי מִילֵּי לְעִנְיַן אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the proof of step 24 by limiting its scope.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's use of the 'עמך' ברייתא to prove leniency for redemption.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Leniency about living conditions does not have to carry over to redemption, where there may be a reason for strictness.

steps.title: רבי יוסי begins: how severe is שביעית
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting the ברייתא of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא about how serious it is to treat שביעית lightly.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי יוסי son of רבי חנינא says: Come and see how severe even the 'dust' of the Sabbatical Year is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting the source behind the scholar's strict view. This is only the opening line; the ברייתא continues in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי teaches that even a light violation of שביעית brings serious results. The full ברייתא, which follows, will show how this connects to selling oneself as a slave and why redemption might be strict.

keyTerms.meaning: Its 'dust', meaning even a small or light violation

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it was taught: Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina says:
Come and see
how severe the "dust" of the Sabbatical Year is:
phrases.notes: 'Dust' means even a small brush with the laws of שביעית, not just a full violation.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אוֹמֵר: בֹּא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה קָשֶׁה אֲבָקָהּ שֶׁל שְׁבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins quoting the source named in step 25 as the reason for strictness.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a reason to be strict with the slave regarding redemption.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא about the severity of שביעית (continues in steps 27-40).

steps.title: Trading in שביעית produce leads to selling movable property
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: one who does business with שביעית produce will end up selling his movable things. This is learned from the פסוק next to the יובל פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person who does business with שביעית produce will end up selling his movable things. It says, 'In this יובל year you shall return every man to his land,' and right next to it, 'And if you sell something to your neighbor or buy from your neighbor's hand.' That means something acquired by passing it from hand to hand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא that it started in the last step. This is the first rung of the downward ladder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Doing business with שביעית fruit is forbidden. The ברייתא learns the punishment from the order of the פסוקים: the יובל פסוק is followed by a פסוק about selling. The words 'from your neighbor's hand' point to things passed hand to hand, which means movable property.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce of the seventh year, which may not be traded
Right next to it (the next פסוק)
The fiftieth year, when land returns to its owner

steps.whyThisMatters: This chain of losses builds toward a person selling himself. The scholar needs that to argue that an עבד עברי got there through sin, so maybe we should be strict with him.

phrases.english: If a person does business with שביעית produce,
in the end he sells his movable things,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״בִּשְׁנַת הַיּוֹבֵל תָּשֻׁבוּ אִישׁ אֶל אֲחֻזָּתוֹ״,
phrases.english: as it says: 'In this יובל year you shall return every man to his land,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:13

phrases.english: and right next to it:
'And if you sell something to your neighbor
or buy from your neighbor's hand' —
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:14

phrases.english: something acquired from hand to hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quotation begun in step 26.
steps.raayaObject: The scholar's claim (step 25) that the Torah may be strict with an עבד עברי when it comes to redemption.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, based on ויקרא 25:13-14.

steps.title: If he does not repent, he sells his fields and then his house
steps.stepSummary: If he ignores the warning, he sells his fields. If he still does not repent, he sells his house. Each step comes from a פסוק in ויקרא 25.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not sense it, in the end he sells his fields, as it says, 'If your brother becomes poor and sells some of his land.' If it did not come to his hand, he ends up selling his house, as it says, 'If a man sells a house in a walled city.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds the next two rungs of the ladder: fields, then house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each loss is worse than the one before, and each one follows the order of the פסוקים in ויקרא 25. Notice that the wording changes. First it says 'he did not sense', then 'it did not come to his hand'. The גמרא asks about this change in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He did not sense (that he was being punished)
It did not come to his hand (he did not take hold of תשובה)

phrases.english: If he did not sense it,
in the end he sells his fields,
as it says: 'If your brother becomes poor and sells some of his land.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:25

phrases.english: If it did not come to his hand,
phrases.notes: Meaning: he still didn't reach out and grab hold of תשובה.

phrases.english: it goes on until he sells his house,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״כִּי יִמְכֹּר בֵּית מוֹשַׁב עִיר חוֹמָה״.
phrases.english: as it says: 'If a man sells a house to live in, in a walled city.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:29

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא הִרְגִּישׁ – לְסוֹף מוֹכֵר אֶת שְׂדוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with the next stages of loss.
steps.raayaObject: The scholar's claim that the Torah may be strict with an עבד עברי when it comes to redemption.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, based on ויקרא 25:25 and 25:29.

steps.title: Why does the wording change?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא first says 'he did not sense' and later says 'it did not come to his hand'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different there, where it says 'he did not sense', and what is different here, where it says 'it did not come to his hand'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses the quote to ask about a change in wording inside the ברייתא. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack. It is a request to explain why the ברייתא used two different phrases for what looks like the same failure to repent.

phrases.english: What is different there,
where it says 'he did not sense,'
and what is different here,
where it says 'it did not come to his hand'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pauses the ברייתא to ask about its wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ברייתא switches from 'לא הרגיש' to 'לא באת לידו'.

steps.title: רב הונא: a repeated sin becomes permitted to him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with רב הונא: once a person sins and repeats the sin, it is permitted to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It follows רב הונא, who said: once a person commits a sin and repeats it, it is permitted to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the wording question by quoting a rule of רב הונא about repeated sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the second time, the sinner no longer feels he is doing anything wrong. So the ברייתא can't talk about him 'not sensing' anymore. Of course he doesn't sense it. Instead it says repentance 'did not come to his hand'.

keyTerms.meaning: In line with רב הונא's statement

phrases.english: It is like רב הונא,
for רב הונא said:
once a person commits a sin
and repeats it,
it is permitted to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: By the second sin, the person no longer feels it is wrong, so the ברייתא changes its wording.

steps.title: Can a sin really become permitted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא is surprised: could it really be that repeating a sin makes it permitted?
steps.simpleTranslation: 'It is permitted to him' — could you really think that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא objects to the literal wording of רב הונא's rule. This sets up a correction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, רב הונא would be saying that sinning twice makes the act allowed, which is impossible. So the גמרא challenges the words, not the idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Could it enter your mind? (this can't be right)

phrases.english: 'It is permitted to him' — could you think that?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the literal wording of רב הונא's rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'הותרה לו' in רב הונא's rule.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sin can't actually become permitted just because it was repeated.

steps.title: It only feels permitted to him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the wording: the sin becomes to him like something permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it becomes to him like something permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes רב הונא's wording. The sin is not really allowed; it just feels allowed to the sinner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The change is about how the sinner feels, not about the law. This keeps the answer to the wording question in place: after a repeated sin the person doesn't sense any wrongdoing.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: once someone repeats a sin, it starts to feel permitted to him. That is why the ברייתא switches from 'he did not sense' to 'it did not come to his hand'.

phrases.english: Rather, it becomes to him like something permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 31 by rewording רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sin only feels permitted to the sinner.

steps.title: If he still does not repent, he sells his daughter
steps.stepSummary: Back to the ברייתא: if he still does not repent, he ends up selling his daughter as a maidservant.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it did not come to his hand, it goes on until he sells his daughter, as it says, 'And if a man sells his daughter as a maidservant.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to quoting the ברייתא and adds the next, even worse rung: selling his daughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The losses have moved from property to his own family. This is the first sale of a person in the chain.

keyTerms.meaning: A maidservant (here, a Jewish girl sold by her father)

phrases.english: If it did not come to his hand,
it goes on until he sells his daughter,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְכִי יִמְכֹּר אִישׁ אֶת בִּתּוֹ לְאָמָה״,
phrases.english: as it says: 'And if a man sells his daughter as a maidservant,'
phrases.notes: שמות 21:7

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ עַד שֶׁמּוֹכֵר אֶת בִּתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the wording side discussion to the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: The scholar's claim that the Torah may be strict with an עבד עברי when it comes to redemption.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, based on שמות 21:7.

steps.title: Why selling a daughter appears in this chain
steps.stepSummary: The daughter פסוק is not in this section of the Torah, but the ברייתא includes it to teach that a person would sooner sell his daughter than borrow with interest.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though 'his daughter' is not written in this section, it teaches us this: a person will sell his daughter rather than borrow with interest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ברייתא jumped to a פסוק from a different place in the Torah. It is answering a question it never says out loud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All the earlier rungs came from ויקרא 25, but selling a daughter is in שמות. The ברייתא still puts it here to teach a practical lesson: borrowing with interest is worse than selling a daughter.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us

phrases.english: And even though 'his daughter'
is not written in this section,
phrases.notes: The earlier sales all came from ויקרא 25, but the daughter פסוק is in שמות.

phrases.english: it teaches us this:
a person will sell his daughter
rather than borrow with interest.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּבִתּוֹ לָא כְּתִיבָא בְּהַאי עִנְיָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the daughter פסוק just quoted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Selling a daughter is preferable to borrowing with interest.

steps.title: A daughter's debt shrinks, interest keeps growing
steps.stepSummary: The reason: a sold daughter works off her price and goes free, but an interest debt keeps getting bigger.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? His daughter's debt goes down and she goes free, but this keeps growing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the lesson and gives it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jewish maidservant's remaining price gets smaller over time until she leaves. Interest is the opposite: the debt gets larger the longer it stays unpaid.
steps.whatToRemember: A person would sooner sell his daughter than borrow with interest, because her debt gets smaller over time while interest keeps growing.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
His daughter's debt goes down and she goes free,
but this keeps on growing.
phrases.notes: 'This' means the interest debt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the lesson in step 34.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A daughter's debt shrinks and ends, while interest keeps growing.

steps.title: Next stage: he borrows with interest
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if he still does not do תשובה, he ends up borrowing with רבית. It proves this from the פסוק about a poor brother, which sits right next to the ban on taking interest.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he still does not do תשובה, he ends up borrowing with interest. The פסוק says: 'And if your brother grows poor and his means fail with you,' and right next to it: 'Do not take from him' interest.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's list of punishments after its side-point about the daughter. The next stage down is borrowing money with רבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the פסוקים in ויקרא כ״ה in order, as a story of a man getting poorer step by step. The proof comes from סמיכות, two פסוקים placed next to each other. The poor brother in פסוק 35 is followed by the interest ban in פסוק 36, so the next thing that happens to him is a loan with interest.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'it did not come to his hand'; here it means he still did not do תשובה.
Interest on a loan, which the Torah forbids between Jews.
'Placed right next to it'; learning from two פסוקים that stand side by side.
'Grows poor'; the word that opens several of the פסוקים in this spiral.

phrases.english: If no [repentance] comes to his hand,
phrases.notes: The word 'repentance' is left out but understood. It means he still has not done תשובה.

phrases.english: he ends up borrowing with interest,
as it says: 'And if your brother grows poor
and his means fail with you,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:35

phrases.english: and right next to it is written:
'Do not take from him,' etc.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:36. The rest of the פסוק finishes the thought: do not take interest from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ עַד שֶׁלֹּוֶה בְּרִבִּית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side-point in steps 34-35 to the ברייתא's list of stages, picking up after the sale of the daughter.
steps.raayaObject: That the next stage of the spiral is borrowing with רבית.

steps.title: Next stage: he sells himself
steps.stepSummary: If he still does not do תשובה, he ends up selling himself as a slave. The proof is the פסוק 'and if your brother grows poor and sells himself to you.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If he still does not do תשובה, he ends up selling himself, as the פסוק says: 'And if your brother grows poor and sells himself to you.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves one step lower. Now the man has nothing left to sell, so he sells himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the next 'וכי ימוך' פסוק in the same פרשה, פסוק 39. It's the same pattern as before: he still hasn't done תשובה, so he falls one more stage and must sell his own body as an עבד עברי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he is sold' or 'sells himself'; the word in the פסוק.
A Jewish servant who was sold for a set time.

phrases.english: If [repentance] still does not come to his hand,
he ends up selling himself,
as it says: 'And if your brother grows poor
and sells himself to you.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:39

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא בָּאת לְיָדוֹ עַד שֶׁמּוֹכֵר אֶת עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The next, lower stage after borrowing with interest.
steps.raayaObject: That after the interest stage he ends up selling himself.

steps.title: Sold not to a Jew, but to a גר תושב
steps.stepSummary: He is not even sold to a fellow Jew. He is sold to a גר, and not to a גר צדק but to a גר תושב, as the פסוק says.
steps.simpleTranslation: Not to you, but to a גר, as it says 'to a גר.' And not to a righteous convert, but to a גר תושב, as it says 'a גר תושב.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא shows how far he falls even after selling himself. The buyer gets further and further from the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being sold to a Jew is bad, but being sold to a גר is worse. The פסוק adds the word 'תושב', which shows this is not a גר צדק, a full convert. It is a גר תושב, a non-Jew who only keeps the seven מצוות בני נח. That is a deeper fall.

keyTerms.meaning: A full, righteous convert to Judaism.
A non-Jew living in ארץ ישראל who accepted the seven מצוות בני נח, but did not convert.
'Not this, but even that'; showing an even worse level.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up a גר צדק with a גר תושב. A גר צדק is a full Jew. A גר תושב is still a non-Jew, and that is why being sold to him is a worse fall.

phrases.english: Not [only] to you, but even to a stranger,
as it says: 'to a stranger,'
and not to a righteous convert,
but even to a resident non-Jew,
as it says: 'a stranger who is a settler.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:47

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes deeper into the sale stage: who ends up buying him.
steps.raayaObject: That he is sold to a גר תושב, not just to a Jew or a גר צדק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words ״לגר״ and ״גר תושב״ in ויקרא 25:47.

steps.title: ״משפחת גר״ means a נכרי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains the next words of the פסוק: 'a stranger's family' refers to a נכרי, a plain non-Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A stranger's family': this is a non-Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the next phrase in the same פסוק. It shows he can fall even lower and be sold to a full non-Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גר תושב at least keeps the seven מצוות בני נח. The phrase 'משפחת גר' points to a נכרי who has not accepted even that much. This is the next rung down.

keyTerms.meaning: 'A stranger's family'; the next words in ויקרא 25:47.
A non-Jew who did not take on the מצוות of a גר תושב.

phrases.english: 'A stranger's family': this is a non-Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the next phrase of the same פסוק to show an even lower buyer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״משפחת גר״ refers to a נכרי, so he may even be sold to a full non-Jew.

steps.title: Starting to explain ״לעקר״
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא begins to explain the last word of the פסוק, ״לעקר״ (an offshoot). The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says: 'to an offshoot'...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The ברייתא quotes the word ״לעקר״ and is about to explain what it adds; the answer comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern so far is that each new word in the פסוק shows a lower level of buyer. So the learner should expect ״לעקר״ to show the very lowest level, which the next lines will spell out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When it says'; a formula that introduces the explanation of a word in the פסוק.
'Offshoot' or 'root'; the last word of ויקרא 25:47.

phrases.english: When it says: 'to an offshoot' [of a stranger's family],

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the final word of the same פסוק, setting up its explanation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Introduces the word ״לעקר״ as another level of the fall, to be explained next.
